newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Acer denies patent infringement charge.
newsitem.headline: Acer denies patent infringement charge.

text.p: Taiwan's leading computer maker, Acer Inc, on Wednesday denied a patent infringement charge filed by U.S.-based Lucent Technologies.
Acer said Lucent had contacted the firm to see whether Acer was interested in using some of its patents.

"Lucent's patent rights involved voice communications and processing technology of voice and video, which had no direct connection with Acer's main product -- personal computers," Acer said in a statement.
But it did not specify whether it had adopted any patents from Lucent.
"As for the issues related to patent infringement, Acer believes it did not violate (Lucent's) related patent rights," it said.
Lucent said the suit charges Acer with violating eight patents relating to semiconductor manufacturing technologies, speech and video coding, and computer display technologies.
Lucent added the suit affects Acer's desktop and laptop computers.

Lucent said it filed the suit in the U.S. District Court in Delaware and named as defendants Acer Inc of Taiwan, Acer America Corp and Acer Laboratories Inc of San Jose, California, and Acer Peripherals Labs Inc of Santa Clara, California.
Acer said it had not received the suit, but added it had a longstanding tradition for respecting intellectual property rights.
